column1: # Parity cases that stop on a typed refusal on the Rust arm although the Rust engine serves the member (or the case's setup step was refused). Edited by hand.
# One file per owner (test/rust-stop-pins/<owner>.tsv); every file is read, so an owner adds or removes only its own rows.
# Columns (tab separated): parity file, case name, member that refused, owner, due date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC), what Rust declines.
# A row lets the case stop on that member's typed refusal (GBRAIN_TEST_RUST_ARM=1). The run fails when the case stops on another member, when the
# due date has passed (the row goes red at 00:00 UTC on the day after the due date), or when the case no longer stops (remove the row).

column2: the foreign keys read from the catalog; a store that keeps no list of them refuses by name

column6: By design, not a bug: the Rust store keeps no foreign-key list (each family checks its references in code), so listCatalogForeignKeys refuses by name (raw_sql) before any work and never answers an empty list. Only engine graduation through the SQL catalog reads it (copyOrder stops earlier at the relation set; fkClosure and verifyForeignKeys stop here); no swap or shadow step does. Review on 2027-03-01, after the post-Dec-1 managed-mode program, or earlier when gbrain migrate --to rust (RUST_ENGINE.md PR 21) needs the list: then the store records its references as data and this row goes.
